title: Module 2 · Vancomycin and Aminoglycoside Dosing
intro: Vancomycin AUC dosing with full worked math, loading doses, obesity, dialysis, continuous infusion, children, oral vancomycin, and aminoglycosides: dosing weight, Hartford, traditional levels, synergy and toxicity.

cases.title: Why vancomycin needs a pharmacist
cases.stem: A 62 year old man has MRSA in 2 of 2 blood cultures. The team orders "vancomycin per pharmacy." This is the first time you dose it alone.

steps.q: What does vancomycin exposure need to reach for serious MRSA infection?

options.t: AUC24 of 400 to 600 (assuming MIC 1)
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 1.

options.t: Trough of 15 to 20 mcg/mL
options.why: The 2009 trough target; no longer recommended for serious MRSA because it overshoots AUC and raises kidney injury.

options.t: Trough of 10 to 15 mcg/mL
options.why: Older target for less serious infections; troughs are no longer the dosing goal.

options.t: AUC24 of 600 to 800 (assuming MIC 1)
options.why: Above 600 is where kidney injury risk climbs.

steps.teach: Vancomycin is **time and exposure dependent**. Think "area under the curve," the total drug the bug sees over a day, not one number at one moment.
steps.where: Rybak 2020 consensus guideline, Recommendation 1. St. Mary's pharmacy to dose policy tells you what software or method you use.

steps.q: What is the preferred way to estimate AUC?

options.t: Bayesian software with one or two levels
options.why: Preferred.

options.t: Two levels (peak and trough) with first order equations
options.why: Acceptable alternative.

options.t: A single trough compared with 15 to 20 mcg/mL
options.why: Trough only monitoring is no longer recommended.

options.t: A single peak 1 hour after the infusion
options.why: A peak alone cannot estimate AUC without a model.

steps.q: When should the AUC target be reached?

options.t: Within the first 24 to 48 hours
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 3.

options.t: Within the first 72 to 96 hours
options.why: Too slow for bacteremia.

options.t: At the third or fourth dose, at steady state only
options.why: Steady state helps two level math, but Bayesian tools let you dose earlier.

options.t: Within 7 days, before the first weekly review
options.why: Far too late.

cases.monitor: Serum creatinine at least daily early on, urine output, AUC estimate once and again if kidney function changes, blood cultures until negative.
cases.pearl: **Vanc target: AUC 400 to 600, early, by Bayesian or two levels. No more trough only to 15 to 20.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: The loading dose
cases.stem: An 80 kg woman in septic shock. CrCl about 35 mL/min and falling. The resident wants to "reduce the first dose because of her kidneys."

steps.q: Should the first (loading) dose be reduced for her kidney function?

options.t: No: the load depends on body size, not kidneys
options.why: Load by weight, maintain by kidneys.

options.t: Yes: cut the load in half when CrCl is under 50
options.why: Halving is a maintenance adjustment idea, never for the load.

options.t: Yes: give 15 mg/kg instead of 25 mg/kg
options.why: 15 mg/kg is a maintenance dose size, not a reduced load.

options.t: No load: start maintenance every 24 hours
options.why: Critically ill patients benefit most from a load.

steps.teach: **Load by weight, maintain by kidneys.** That one sentence prevents a very common error.

steps.q: What loading dose range does the guideline allow, and what maximum?

options.t: 20 to 35 mg/kg actual weight, max 3,000 mg
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 10.

options.t: 20 to 25 mg/kg actual weight, max 3,000 mg
options.why: That narrower range is the obesity recommendation.

options.t: 15 to 20 mg/kg actual weight, max 2,000 mg
options.why: 15 to 20 mg/kg is the maintenance dose and the continuous infusion load.

options.t: 25 mg/kg actual weight, then 7.5 to 10 mg/kg
options.why: That is the hemodialysis load and maintenance.

steps.q: You choose 2,000 mg. By the FDA label rate (no faster than 10 mg/min), how long is the minimum infusion?

options.t: 200 minutes (3 hours 20 minutes)
options.why: 2,000 mg / 10 mg/min.

options.t: 120 minutes (2 hours)
options.why: That follows a 1 g per hour policy, not the 10 mg/min label rate.

options.t: 60 minutes (1 hour)
options.why: 60 minutes is the label minimum for doses up to about 600 mg at 10 mg/min.

options.t: 100 minutes (1 hour 40 minutes)
options.why: That is 1,000 mg at 10 mg/min.

steps.teach: Infusion time is a safety check you do on every vancomycin order. Fast infusion causes flushing, itching and low BP (infusion reaction, not a true allergy).
steps.where: Vancomycin label, Dosage and Administration. St. Mary's IV administration guide for the local rate.

cases.call: **S/B:** Septic shock, 80 kg, CrCl 35 and falling, vancomycin ordered. **A:** The loading dose should not be reduced for kidney function. **R:** I recommend 2,000 mg IV now (25 mg/kg), then I will choose the maintenance dose by kidney function and check levels in the first 24 to 48 hours.
cases.pearl: **Load by weight (20 to 35 mg/kg, max 3 g). Maintain by kidneys.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864
Vancomycin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)
St. Mary's pharmacy to dose vancomycin and aminoglycoside protocol (verify locally)

workup.calc: Load for 80 kg: 20 to 25 mg/kg = 1,600 to 2,000 mg (guideline range 20 to 35, max 3,000). 2,000 mg at 10 mg/min = 200 minutes minimum by label.

cases.title: Empiric maintenance dose
cases.stem: A 58 year old man, 72 kg, SCr 1.0 mg/dL, normal and stable. MRSA osteomyelitis. You need a starting maintenance dose.

steps.q: Calculate his CrCl (Cockcroft Gault).

options.t: About 82 mL/min
About 70 mL/min
options.why: That applies the 0.85 female factor to a man.

options.t: About 58 mL/min
options.why: That subtracts age from 116 instead of 140.

options.t: About 98 mL/min
options.why: That uses an SCr of about 0.8.

steps.q: Which starting regimen fits the usual adult range (15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours)?

options.t: 1,250 mg every 12 hours (about 17 mg/kg)
options.why: Inside 15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours.

options.t: 1,250 mg every 24 hours (about 17 mg/kg)
options.why: Every 24 hours fits reduced kidney function, not CrCl 82.

options.t: 1,750 mg every 12 hours (about 24 mg/kg)
options.why: Above the 20 mg/kg maintenance range; 25 mg/kg is a loading dose size.

options.t: 750 mg every 12 hours (about 10 mg/kg)
options.why: 10 mg/kg is the high flux dialysis maintenance size.

steps.q: When will you get levels?

options.t: Early, so AUC is known within 24 to 48 hours
options.why: Serious infection and a long course need AUC monitoring.

options.t: Only if creatinine rises during treatment
options.why: Waiting for injury is too late.

options.t: Weekly, starting at the end of week one
options.why: Weekly pre dialysis levels apply to hemodialysis, not here.

options.t: Never, because his kidneys are normal
options.why: Long serious courses need monitoring.

cases.pearl: **15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours to start, then let the levels decide.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864
St. Mary's pharmacy to dose vancomycin and aminoglycoside protocol (verify locally)

workup.calc: CrCl = (140 minus 58) x 72 / (72 x 1.0) = **82 mL/min**. 1,250 mg every 12 hours = 17.4 mg/kg per dose: inside 15 to 20 mg/kg.

cases.title: Calculating AUC with two levels
cases.stem: Vancomycin 1,000 mg IV every 12 hours, infused over 1 hour, at steady state. Peak drawn 1 hour after the end of the infusion (2 hours after the start): **30 mcg/mL**. Trough drawn 30 minutes before the next dose (11.5 hours after the start): **10 mcg/mL**.

steps.q: Step 1: calculate the elimination rate constant (ke).

options.why: Time between draws: 11.5 minus 2 = 9.5 hours.
Uses the dosing interval instead of the time between the two draws.

options.t: (30 minus 10) / 9.5 h = 2.1 per hour
options.why: Elimination is exponential; you need the natural log of the ratio.
ke uses the natural log, not log base 10.

steps.teach: **ke = ln(C1 / C2) / time between the draws.** Half life = 0.693 / ke. Here half life is about 6 hours.

steps.q: Step 2: estimate the true peak at the end of the infusion (1 hour after the start).

options.t: About 33.7 mcg/mL
30 mcg/mL (as drawn)
options.why: The draw was 1 hour after the infusion ended; the true end of infusion peak is higher.

options.t: About 37.8 mcg/mL
options.why: Extrapolates back 2 hours (to the start of the infusion) instead of 1.

options.t: About 26.7 mcg/mL
options.why: Extrapolates in the wrong direction (forward in time).

steps.q: Step 3: estimate the true trough at the end of the interval (12 hours).

options.t: About 9.4 mcg/mL
10 mcg/mL (as drawn)
options.why: The draw was 30 minutes before the end of the interval.

options.t: About 8.9 mcg/mL
options.why: Extrapolates forward 1 hour instead of 30 minutes.

options.t: About 10.6 mcg/mL
options.why: Extrapolates in the wrong direction.

steps.q: Step 4: calculate AUC for one dose, then AUC over 24 hours. Infusion part = infusion time x (Cmax + Cmin) / 2. Elimination part = (Cmax minus Cmin) / ke.

options.t: About 462 (231 per dose x 2)
options.why: Infusion part 21.6 + elimination part 209.6 = 231 per 12 hours.

options.t: About 231 (one dose only)
options.why: That is one interval; multiply by 24/12.

options.t: About 384 (drawn levels, no extrapolation)
options.why: Using the drawn 30 and 10 underestimates the true area.

options.t: About 924 (231 x 4)
options.why: Multiplied by 4 doses; every 12 hours is 2 doses per day.

steps.q: AUC24 is about 462. What do you do?

options.t: Continue the regimen; keep watching kidney function
options.why: 462 is inside 400 to 600.

options.t: Increase the dose: the trough of 10 is below 15
options.why: Trough thinking; the AUC is on target.

options.t: Decrease the dose: AUC above 400 raises kidney risk
options.why: Risk climbs above 600, not 400.

options.t: Change to every 8 hours to raise the trough
options.why: Same trough error; AUC is on target.

steps.teach: A trough of 10 can go with a perfect AUC. Pushing the trough to 15 to 20 would push this AUC far over 600.

cases.pearl: **ke = ln(C1/C2)/time. Extrapolate to true Cmax and Cmin. AUC = infusion part + elimination part, times doses per day.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Adjusting to the target
cases.stem: On vancomycin 1,000 mg every 12 hours, the Bayesian estimate is AUC24 = 320. Kidney function is stable. Goal AUC about 500.

steps.q: Vancomycin follows linear kinetics. What new total dose reaches about 500?

options.t: 1,500 mg every 12 hours (predicted AUC about 480)
1,250 mg every 12 hours (predicted AUC about 400)
options.why: Lands on the bottom edge of the range, below the 500 goal.

options.t: 2,000 mg every 12 hours (predicted AUC about 640)
options.why: Above 600: kidney injury risk.

options.t: 1,500 mg every 24 hours (predicted AUC about 240)
options.why: Halves the daily exposure.

steps.teach: **New dose = old dose x (target AUC / current AUC).** Round to a measurable dose and recheck after the change.

steps.q: When do you recheck exposure after a dose change?

options.t: Near the new steady state, and whenever kidneys change
options.why: Bayesian tools allow earlier checks.

options.t: Only at the end of the planned course
options.why: Too late to adjust.

options.t: Every day for the whole course
options.why: More often than needed when stable.

options.t: Never again once one AUC is on target
options.why: Kidney function changes during illness.

cases.pearl: **Linear: new dose = old dose x target / current.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Too much exposure
cases.stem: Day 5 of vancomycin and piperacillin tazobactam for a diabetic foot infection. SCr rose from 0.9 to 1.5 mg/dL. Estimated AUC24 is 780.

steps.q: What is happening?

options.t: AUC above 600 with early kidney injury
options.why: SCr up about 67%.

options.t: Expected creatinine rise from piperacillin tazobactam alone
options.why: The combination is linked to AKI, but the AUC of 780 is the fixable part.

options.t: Contrast nephropathy from a recent scan
options.why: Possible contributor; nothing in the case suggests contrast.

options.t: Lab variation; repeat the SCr in a week
options.why: A 67% rise meets the AKI definition.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Hold the next dose, recheck a level, restart lower by AUC
Ask whether MRSA coverage is still needed
options.why: Stopping vancomycin is the best kidney protection.

options.t: Ask about changing pip tazo (for example to cefepime)
options.why: The combination is linked to more AKI in observational studies.

options.t: Add furosemide to flush the kidneys
options.why: Loop diuretics do not protect kidneys and add ototoxicity with aminoglycosides.

options.t: Switch to a continuous infusion at the same daily dose
options.why: Same daily exposure, same AUC.

steps.q: How strong is the evidence that piperacillin tazobactam increases vancomycin kidney injury?

options.t: Mostly observational; reported to raise the risk
options.why: Rybak 2020 language.

options.t: Proven by several large randomized trials
options.why: No large RCT proves it.

options.t: Disproven; the creatinine rise is only a lab effect
options.why: Debated, not disproven.

options.t: Shown only in children, not adults
options.why: Signals exist in both.

cases.call: **S/B:** Day 5 vancomycin plus pip tazo, SCr 0.9 to 1.5, AUC 780. **A:** Exposure is above target and kidney injury is starting. **R:** I recommend holding tonight's dose, a level in the morning, and restarting at a lower dose. Do the cultures still support MRSA coverage? If not, can we stop vancomycin?
cases.pearl: **AUC above 600 + rising creatinine = hold, recheck, re dose, and ask if vanc is still needed.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Red man? Infusion reaction
cases.setting: Med surg · 30 minutes into an infusion
cases.stem: A nurse calls: "The vancomycin is running and my patient's face, neck and chest are bright red and itchy. BP 112/70, breathing fine, no wheeze."

steps.q: What is this most likely?

options.t: Vancomycin infusion reaction (rate related)
options.why: Histamine release.

options.t: IgE mediated anaphylaxis needing epinephrine
options.why: No hypotension, wheeze or airway swelling.

options.t: DRESS syndrome from a new drug exposure
options.why: Appears days to weeks into therapy.

options.t: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
options.why: A rare blistering reaction days into therapy.

steps.q: What do you tell the nurse?

options.t: Pause, antihistamine if ordered, restart slower
Document as infusion reaction, not allergy; longer infusion next time
Stop vancomycin permanently and switch to daptomycin
options.why: Not needed for an infusion reaction.

options.t: Give epinephrine 0.5 mg IM now
options.why: That is the anaphylaxis treatment.

cases.pearl: **Red and itchy, BP fine = too fast. Pause, antihistamine, slower.**

sources.t: Vancomycin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)
Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

cases.title: Vancomycin in obesity
cases.stem: A 41 year old woman, 160 kg, CrCl about 120 mL/min, MRSA bacteremia from a skin source.

steps.q: Which loading dose does the guideline suggest in obesity?

options.t: 20 to 25 mg/kg actual weight, max 3,000 mg
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 12.

options.t: 20 to 35 mg/kg actual weight, max 3,000 mg
options.why: That is the general critical illness range.

options.t: 25 mg/kg ideal body weight, no maximum
options.why: Loading uses actual weight, and the cap is 3,000 mg.

options.t: 25 mg/kg adjusted body weight, max 2,000 mg
options.why: Adjusted weight is an aminoglycoside concept.

steps.q: What is a usual ceiling for the empiric daily maintenance total in obese patients?

options.t: Usually 4,500 mg/day or less to start
options.why: Then AUC guides changes.

options.t: Usually 3,000 mg/day or less to start
options.why: 3,000 mg is the single loading dose cap.

options.t: 20 mg/kg every 8 hours by actual weight (9,600 mg/day)
options.why: Clearance does not rise with weight in proportion.

options.t: Usually 2,000 mg/day or less to start
options.why: Underdoses most obese patients with normal kidneys.

cases.pearl: **Obese: load 20 to 25 mg/kg actual (max 3 g), maintenance usually 4.5 g/day or less, then AUC.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864
St. Mary's pharmacy to dose vancomycin and aminoglycoside protocol (verify locally)

workup.calc: 20 mg/kg x 160 kg = 3,200 mg, so the 3,000 mg cap applies. Maintenance usually 4,500 mg/day or less to start, then AUC.

cases.title: Vancomycin and hemodialysis
cases.stem: A 70 kg man on intermittent hemodialysis three times a week (high permeability dialyzer) has an MRSA line infection. Vancomycin is to be given after dialysis.

steps.q: What loading dose does the guideline list after dialysis?

options.t: 25 mg/kg after the session (about 1,750 mg)
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 13.

options.t: 35 mg/kg during the session (high permeability)
options.why: Intradialytic loading is 30 to 35 mg/kg; this dose is given after dialysis.

options.t: 15 mg/kg after the session
options.why: 15 mg/kg is a typical maintenance dose size.

options.t: 5 mg/kg because the kidneys do not work
options.why: The load fills volume regardless of kidneys.

steps.q: What maintenance dose follows, and how is it monitored?

options.t: About 10 mg/kg after each session; pre HD level weekly
options.why: Pre dialysis levels of 15 to 20 likely reach the AUC target.

options.t: About 7.5 mg/kg after each session; pre HD level weekly
options.why: 7.5 mg/kg is for low permeability dialyzers.

options.t: About 15 mg/kg daily with daily troughs
options.why: Dosing follows the dialysis schedule.

options.t: About 25 mg/kg after each session, no levels
options.why: 25 mg/kg is the load.

cases.pearl: **HD: 25 mg/kg load, then about 10 mg/kg after each session (high flux); check pre dialysis levels.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864
St. Mary's pharmacy to dose vancomycin and aminoglycoside protocol (verify locally)

workup.calc: 25 mg/kg x 70 kg = **1,750 mg** after dialysis; then 10 mg/kg = **700 mg** after each session (high permeability).

cases.title: Continuous infusion vancomycin
cases.stem: The ICU uses continuous infusion vancomycin for a 75 kg patient.

steps.q: What does the guideline suggest for loading and maintenance?

options.t: Load 15 to 20 mg/kg, then 30 to 40 mg/kg/day
options.why: Rybak 2020, Recommendation 7 (up to 60 mg/kg/day).

options.t: Load 20 to 35 mg/kg, then 15 to 20 mg/kg every 12 h
options.why: Intermittent dosing.

options.t: No load, then 60 to 80 mg/kg/day
options.why: 60 to 80 mg/kg/day is the pediatric range.

options.t: Load 25 mg/kg, then 10 mg/kg/day
options.why: Close to hemodialysis dosing.

steps.q: The steady state level is 22 mcg/mL. What is the AUC24?

options.t: About 528 (22 x 24)
options.why: Continuous infusion: AUC24 = Css x 24.

options.t: About 264 (22 x 12)
options.why: Multiplies by 12 hours instead of 24.

options.t: About 22 (the level itself)
options.why: The level is not the AUC.
Multiplies by 48 hours.

steps.q: What line issue matters most with continuous vancomycin?

options.t: Y site compatibility with drugs in the line
options.why: It runs all day.

options.t: Light protection for the bag and tubing
options.why: Not required.

options.t: PVC free tubing to prevent adsorption
options.why: Matters for nitroglycerin and insulin.

options.t: A 0.22 micron in line filter
options.why: Needed for phenytoin, not routine here.

cases.pearl: **Continuous vanc: AUC = level x 24. Target level 20 to 25.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

workup.calc: Load 15 to 20 mg/kg x 75 = 1,125 to 1,500 mg; maintenance 30 to 40 mg/kg/day = 2,250 to 3,000 mg/day. AUC24 = level x 24 = 22 x 24 = **528**.

cases.title: Children and vancomycin
cases.stem: A 6 year old, 20 kg, normal kidney function, MRSA osteomyelitis.

steps.q: Which empiric total daily dose range does the guideline suggest for children 3 months and older?

options.t: 60 to 80 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours
options.why: Children 3 months and older (Rybak 2020).

options.t: 45 to 60 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours
options.why: Older empiric dosing the guideline says may be insufficient.

options.t: 15 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 12 hours
options.why: Adult maintenance.

options.t: 30 to 40 mg/kg/day as a continuous infusion
options.why: Adult continuous infusion maintenance.

steps.q: For 20 kg at 60 mg/kg/day every 6 hours, what is each dose?

options.t: 300 mg every 6 hours
400 mg every 6 hours
options.why: That is 80 mg/kg/day, the top of the range, not 60.

options.t: 1,200 mg every 6 hours
options.why: The whole day's dose given four times.

options.t: 400 mg every 8 hours
options.why: That is 60 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours, not every 6.

steps.q: Which reference do you open for pediatric dosing?

options.t: A pediatric reference and St. Mary's pediatric protocol
options.why: Lexicomp Pediatric or Harriet Lane.

options.t: The adult Lexicomp monograph, scaled by weight
options.why: Adult doses do not scale safely.

options.t: NeoFax, since it covers all children
options.why: NeoFax is for neonates.

options.t: The FDA label adult section
options.why: Use the pediatric section or a pediatric reference.

cases.pearl: **Kids clear vanc fast: 60 to 80 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours, then AUC.**

sources.t: Rybak MJ, et al. Therapeutic monitoring of vancomycin for serious MRSA infections: revised consensus guideline (ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP). Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864

workup.calc: 60 mg/kg/day x 20 kg = 1,200 mg/day = **300 mg every 6 hours**; 80 mg/kg/day = 400 mg every 6 hours.

cases.title: Oral vancomycin is a different drug
cases.stem: A patient has a first episode of C. difficile infection. The order reads "vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours."

steps.q: What is wrong?

options.t: IV vancomycin does not reach the colon
options.why: C. difficile needs oral therapy.

options.t: The IV dose is too low; use 1.5 g every 12 hours
options.why: Raising the IV dose still does not reach the colon.

options.t: IV vancomycin is fine but needs an AUC target
options.why: AUC dosing is for systemic infections.

options.t: C. difficile requires IV metronidazole only
options.why: Metronidazole is a fallback; the preferred agents are oral.

steps.q: What does the IDSA/SHEA 2021 update recommend for a first episode?

options.t: Fidaxomicin 200 mg BID x 10 days preferred
options.why: IDSA/SHEA 2021; oral vancomycin 125 mg QID x 10 days is the alternative.

options.t: Oral vancomycin 500 mg QID x 10 days
options.why: 500 mg QID is for fulminant disease.

options.t: Metronidazole 500 mg TID x 10 days
options.why: Only for nonsevere disease when the others are unavailable.

options.t: Pulsed fidaxomicin after 5 days of BID
options.why: Extended pulsed dosing is a recurrence option.

cases.call: **S/B:** First C. diff episode, IV vancomycin ordered. **A:** IV vancomycin does not reach the colon. **R:** Change to fidaxomicin 200 mg PO twice daily for 10 days, or vancomycin 125 mg PO four times daily for 10 days if fidaxomicin is not available.
cases.pearl: **C. diff = oral vancomycin (or fidaxomicin). IV vanc does nothing in the colon.**

sources.t: Johnson S, et al. IDSA/SHEA 2021 focused update: C. difficile infection in adults. Clin Infect Dis 2021;73:e1029-e1044

cases.title: How aminoglycosides kill
cases.stem: You are about to verify your first gentamicin order.

steps.q: What kind of killing do aminoglycosides show?

options.t: Concentration dependent with a post antibiotic effect
Time dependent, like beta lactams
options.why: Beta lactams depend on time above MIC.

options.t: AUC dependent with no post antibiotic effect
options.why: AUC/MIC describes vancomycin.

options.t: Bacteriostatic, needing constant levels
options.why: Aminoglycosides are bactericidal.

steps.q: What are the main toxicities?

options.t: Kidney injury (usually reversible)
Ototoxicity (often irreversible)
Neuromuscular blockade
Vancomycin infusion reaction
options.why: Vancomycin only.

options.t: QT prolongation
options.why: A fluoroquinolone and macrolide concern.

steps.q: Which drugs add to aminoglycoside toxicity?

options.t: Loop diuretics (ears)
Vancomycin, amphotericin B, contrast, NSAIDs (kidneys)
Rifampin (induces aminoglycoside metabolism)
options.why: Aminoglycosides are not metabolized; they are cleared unchanged by the kidneys.

options.t: Proton pump inhibitors (reduce absorption)
options.why: IV aminoglycosides are not absorbed from the gut anyway.

cases.pearl: **Big peak, long break. Watch kidneys, ears, and paralytics.**

sources.t: Gentamicin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)
Nicolau DP, et al. Experience with a once daily aminoglycoside program (Hartford). Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995;39:650-655

cases.title: Which weight for gentamicin?
cases.stem: A man 5 ft 10 in, actual weight 110 kg, SCr 0.9. Gentamicin extended interval dosing is planned.

steps.q: Calculate his ideal body weight (male: 50 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 feet).

options.t: 73 kg

options.why: Female formula (45.5 base).
That is his adjusted body weight.
Uses 2.54 (cm per inch) instead of 2.3 kg per inch.

steps.q: His actual weight is 151% of ideal. Which weight do you dose on?

options.t: Adjusted: 73 + 0.4 x 37 = about 88 kg
options.why: Above about 120% of ideal.

options.t: Actual: 110 kg
options.why: Overdoses obese patients.

options.t: Ideal: 73 kg
options.why: Underdoses; some extra body water comes with extra weight.

options.t: Adjusted: 73 + 0.25 x 37 = about 82 kg
options.why: 0.25 is a factor some protocols use for other drugs; aminoglycosides use 0.4.

steps.teach: Know three weights cold: **actual, ideal, adjusted.** Write all three in your note.

steps.q: What is the 7 mg/kg dose?

options.t: About 615 mg (7 x 87.8)
options.why: Round per protocol.

options.t: About 770 mg (7 x 110)
options.why: Actual weight.

options.t: About 511 mg (7 x 73)
options.why: Ideal weight.

options.t: About 439 mg (5 x 87.8)
options.why: 5 mg/kg is the once daily intraamniotic infection dose.

cases.pearl: **IBW: 50 (men) or 45.5 (women) + 2.3 per inch over 5 ft. Obese: adjusted = IBW + 0.4 x excess.**

sources.t: Nicolau DP, et al. Experience with a once daily aminoglycoside program (Hartford). Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995;39:650-655

cases.title: Reading the Hartford nomogram
cases.stem: Gentamicin 7 mg/kg was given at 0800. A random level was drawn at 1800.

steps.q: Is the level timing valid for the Hartford nomogram?

options.t: Yes: 10 hours after the start, inside 6 to 14 hours
options.why: Nicolau 1995.

options.t: No: it must be a trough just before the next dose
options.why: Traditional dosing uses troughs; Hartford uses one random level.

options.t: No: it must be drawn 1 to 2 hours after the start
options.why: That is a peak (for vancomycin two level AUC).

options.t: No: it must be drawn 18 to 24 hours after the start
options.why: Outside the nomogram window.

steps.q: The level falls exactly on the line between the q24h and q36h zones. Which interval?

options.t: Every 36 hours (the longer interval)
Every 24 hours (the shorter interval)
options.why: On a line choose the longer.

options.t: Every 48 hours, to be safe
options.why: Skips a zone.

options.t: Repeat the level before choosing
options.why: Not needed; the rule decides.

steps.q: Another patient's level is above the q48h zone. What do you do?

options.t: Hold doses; redose when the level is below 1
options.why: Clearance too slow for the method.

options.t: Give the next dose in 48 hours anyway
options.why: Too much drug still on board.

options.t: Give 3.5 mg/kg every 48 hours instead
options.why: Not a Hartford step.

options.t: Switch to 1 mg/kg every 8 hours now
options.why: That is synergy dosing.

steps.q: Which patients should NOT be dosed with the Hartford method?

options.t: Pregnancy, burns over 20%, ascites, CrCl below 20 or dialysis
options.why: Original exclusions.

options.t: Endocarditis synergy, cystic fibrosis, children
Adults over 65 with normal kidney function
options.why: Age alone was not an exclusion.

options.t: Adults with obesity using adjusted weight
options.why: Obese adults can use Hartford with a dosing weight per protocol.

cases.pearl: **7 mg/kg, one level at 6 to 14 h, on a line pick longer. Know the exclusions.**

cases.title: Traditional gentamicin and levels
cases.stem: A patient with unstable kidney function gets traditional gentamicin every 8 hours (30 minute infusion).

steps.q: When are the peak and trough drawn?

options.t: Peak 30 min after a 30 min infusion; trough before next dose
Peak 1 to 2 hours after the infusion; trough at random
options.why: The 1 to 2 hour peak is the vancomycin AUC draw.

options.t: One random level 6 to 14 hours after the start
options.why: That is Hartford.

options.t: Trough only, 30 minutes before the next dose
options.why: Traditional dosing needs both.

steps.q: What are the usual safety limits on the label for traditional dosing?

options.t: Avoid peaks above 12 and troughs above 2 mcg/mL
options.why: Gentamicin label.

options.t: Avoid peaks above 35 and troughs above 10 mcg/mL
options.why: Those are amikacin label limits.

options.t: Keep troughs at 15 to 20 mcg/mL
options.why: The old vancomycin trough target.

options.t: Keep peaks at 3 to 4 and troughs below 1 mcg/mL
options.why: Synergy targets for endocarditis.

steps.q: Levels: 7.0 mcg/mL drawn 1 hour after the start, 1.2 mcg/mL drawn 8 hours after the start. What is the half life?

options.t: About 2.75 hours
About 3.15 hours
options.why: Uses 8 hours (the interval) instead of 7 hours between draws.

options.t: About 6.4 hours
options.why: Uses log base 10 instead of the natural log.

options.t: About 0.25 hours
options.why: That number is ke, not the half life.

cases.pearl: **Traditional: peak 30 min after a 30 min infusion, trough before the next dose. Label limits: peak 12, trough 2.**

cases.title: Gentamicin for synergy in endocarditis
cases.stem: Enterococcus faecalis endocarditis. The ID team wants ampicillin plus gentamicin.

steps.q: How is synergy dosing different from gram negative dosing?

options.t: 1 mg/kg every 8 hours; peak 3 to 4, trough below 1
options.why: AHA 2015 synergy dosing.

options.t: 7 mg/kg once daily by the Hartford nomogram
options.why: Endocarditis is a Hartford exclusion.

options.t: 5 mg/kg once daily, adjusted by levels
options.why: Gram negative extended interval dosing.

options.t: 2 mg/kg load, then 1.5 mg/kg every 8 hours
options.why: The intraamniotic infection regimen.

steps.q: What alternative avoids aminoglycoside toxicity for E. faecalis endocarditis?

options.t: Ampicillin plus ceftriaxone
Vancomycin plus gentamicin
options.why: Keeps the aminoglycoside and adds vancomycin kidney risk.

options.t: Daptomycin alone
options.why: An option for resistant enterococci, not the standard alternative here.

options.t: Ampicillin plus cefazolin
options.why: Cefazolin lacks the PBP binding that gives ceftriaxone synergy.

cases.pearl: **Synergy gent: about 1 mg/kg every 8 h, peak 3 to 4, trough below 1. Or ampicillin + ceftriaxone.**

sources.t: Baddour LM, et al. Infective endocarditis in adults (AHA 2015). Circulation 2015;132:1435-1486

cases.title: The patient who says "my ears are ringing"
cases.stem: Day 9 of gentamicin for a complicated urinary infection. The patient reports ringing in the ears and feels unsteady walking. She is also on IV furosemide.

steps.q: What is the concern?

options.t: Aminoglycoside ototoxicity, worsened by furosemide
options.why: Cochlear and vestibular.

options.t: Benign positional vertigo unrelated to drugs
options.why: Never assume with an aminoglycoside.

options.t: Furosemide alone; gentamicin does not affect the ear
options.why: Both are ototoxic.

options.t: Vancomycin ototoxicity
options.why: She is not on vancomycin.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Tell the team today; switch if cultures allow
Check levels and kidney function; review furosemide
Suggest an audiology evaluation
Lower the dose by 25% and continue
options.why: Damage may be permanent; stopping beats lowering.

cases.pearl: **Ringing or dizziness on gent = call today. Ear damage may not come back.**

cases.title: Shift simulation: three kinetics calls
cases.stem: Three things land together: (1) a septic ICU patient needs a vancomycin load and no dose is ordered yet; (2) a gentamicin random level came back for a stable pyelonephritis patient; (3) a vancomycin AUC from yesterday reads 455 on a stable patient.

steps.q: What do you do first?

options.t: Order and send the septic patient's vancomycin load
options.why: Time to antibiotics drives survival.

options.t: Plot the gentamicin level first, since it is ready
options.why: The next dose is hours away.

options.t: Document the AUC of 455 first
options.why: On target; routine.

options.t: Call the stable patient's team about the AUC
options.why: Not needed now.

steps.q: Second?

options.t: Plot the gentamicin level and set the next dose time
Write the AUC note for the stable patient
options.why: Last.

options.t: Recheck the septic patient's CrCl
options.why: Maintenance can wait for labs.

options.t: Order a vancomycin trough for the septic patient
options.why: Too early.

steps.q: For the septic patient (90 kg), what loading dose fits?

options.t: 2,000 to 2,250 mg (about 22 to 25 mg/kg)
options.why: Within 20 to 35 mg/kg, under 3,000 mg.

options.t: 1,000 mg, in case her kidneys are poor
options.why: Loads are not reduced for kidneys.
Above the 3,000 mg cap.
15 mg/kg is a maintenance dose.

cases.pearl: **Septic first dose, then level driven next doses, then documentation.**
